title: Nasuni ransomware protection alerts
volume: None on a normal day. Each detected attack and each block makes one detection, in the appliance's case.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Two custom detection rules for Nasuni Edge Appliances, on the third-party alert records the library's Nasuni parsers write from Ransomware Protection notifications. They make a detection when Nasuni detects a ransomware attack on a volume, and when its mitigation policy blocks a client. Each rule matches sensor type Nasuni Edge Appliance only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Nasuni parsers, and turn on Syslog Export for the Edge Appliances to the data collector, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.
- Ransomware Protection must be turned on for the volumes, with a mitigation policy.

How it works:
- The parsers set the title from Nasuni's message: an attack detected, with the user, client address and confidence level, or the mitigation policy blocking a client address.
- The rules take both at any confidence: Nasuni rates a known signature Low, and it still means files are being encrypted.
- Nasuni's antivirus notification goes to the same schema and isn't taken.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 3 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 26 to 27 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The lines went to HTTP Ingest one per request as text, the way a syslog line arrives.

Known gaps:
- The message wording the parsers read is the one Edge Appliance 9.14 and later send; older appliances may not match.
